report.md:
## This week
You posted 12 videos this week. That's the same as last week. But views went down. Last week a normal video got about 2,472 views. This week a normal video only got about 1,838 views. Your best video was the one that starts with "First I went to TikTok and looked up U.G.C." It pulled in 12,100 views, way more than usual. Your weakest was the one that starts with "One of the most freeing things was realizing that I can literally just leave." It only got 1,213 views. You also posted three videos in the last day or two that are still too new to judge yet.

## Is it how you film, or what you say?
Every video you posted this week was talking-head. So this week alone can't tell us if the way you film matters, only what you talk about. Looking across everything you've made, the topic you pick and the call to action you use seem to matter more than how you shoot it or how you open it. But here's the catch: 93 of your 124 videos are talking-head. You haven't really tested other formats enough to know if they'd do better. You also haven't repeated the same script in two different formats yet, so there's no clean side by side proof either way. Right now, what you say and what you ask people to do seems to matter more than how you film it, but format is still mostly untested.

## What is working
Your come-up videos, the ones about how you got started, usually get about twice the views of a normal video. You've posted 22 of these, so that's a real pattern, not luck. Videos with a link in bio call to action get about 18 times your normal views. You've only tried this 6 times, but that jump is huge and worth trusting. Videos that run over 60 seconds get about six times your normal views too, and you've posted 8 of those.

## Try this next week
Film a come-up story that runs over 60 seconds and ends with a link in bio call to action, since each of those three things does well on its own. Take one script and film it two ways, once talking-head and once as a skit or text overlay, since those formats have shown big numbers but you've barely tried them. Post at least one broll or text overlay video this week just to start building real proof on whether format changes your results.

best.md:
This video did really well. It got about three times what a normal video of yours gets.

Your opening line was "First I went to TikTok and looked up U.G.C." This is direct value, and it worked. It tells people exactly what they're about to learn, so they stay to get the steps.

The video kept its promise after that. You walked through the steps one by one, from researching, to Canva, to mass applying for deals. That step-by-step structure gives people a reason to keep watching, because they want the next step.

You had no call to action here. Since this video did so well, that's a missed chance. You could have asked people to comment their biggest UGC question, or follow for more breakdowns like this one.

Next time, try adding a call to action around the middle of the video, right after you give one useful step, not at the very end where most viewers are already gone.

worst.md:
This video did badly. It got 1,213 views, well under what a normal video of yours gets, which is 3,806.

Your opening line was "One of the most freeing things was realizing that I can literally just leave." That is a decent contradiction style hook, but it did not stop the scroll here. Videos with this same hook style usually land around 3,170 views for you, so even your typical result for this style is below your normal. This one fell way short of even that.

After the opening, the video kept going with one idea: you are allowed to leave a job, a man, a situation. It stays on that one thought the whole time. There is not much new information or a turn to keep people watching past the first few seconds.

There was no call to action here. That is a missed chance. You could have asked people to comment on what they need to leave, or asked them to share this with someone who needs to hear it.

Next time, try adding a specific detail or story in the first 3 seconds, like naming the exact moment you realized you could leave, so people need to know what happens next.
